text_blocks.snippet: A 401(a) plan is generally taxed like a traditional 401(k). Contributions are typically made pre-tax, meaning they reduce your current taxable income, and the money grows tax-deferred until withdrawn in retirement. Upon withdrawal, usually after age 59 1/2, the distributions are taxed as ordinary income. Early withdrawals (before 59 1/2) may also be subject to a 10% penalty, with some exceptions.
